correctness.rationale: For p±=(1±x)/2, the two-copy diagonal input distributions have trace distance x, whereas the normalized-square target outputs differ by 2x/(1+x²). Any single CPTP map has output separation <=x. Triangle inequality with uniform error δ forces δ>=x(1-x²)/(2(1+x²)). Its derivative has sign 1-4x²-x⁴; maximize at x²=sqrt5-2, giving δ*=(sqrt5-1)/4 sqrt(sqrt5-2). The channel discarding one of two input copies returns rho_p with error |p-f(p)| exactly the same bound. Hence minimax equality for ALL deterministic CPTP maps, not just diagonal channels. Independently verified exact symbolic identities and constant.
risk: An equivalent exact deficiency/minimax computation might be known in quantum statistical experiments or approximate nonlinear channel maps with different terminology.
The theorem is exclusively N=2, one-qubit commuting p-family, deterministic CPTP outputs and trace distance; it says nothing about postselected protocols or signed estimators.
